predictions.title: Mistral Workflows tenancy clause enters EU central-government RFPs by Q1 2027
predictions.body: By Q1 2027 the May 9 Mistral AI Workflows day-nine sovereign-cloud landing — France's Direction Generale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) selecting Workflows for tax-return anomaly-detection routing across the central tax-administration estate with the Workflows control-plane separation architecture plus sovereign-cloud execution-worker model explicitly named as procurement deciders over LangGraph self-hosted plus the Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 registry, paid Workflows tenancy lifting to 296 enterprise customers (vs 290 Friday) with daily-execution count crossing 4.4M, and the parallel Workflows-Codestral integration note showing per-step token-budget bookkeeping interoperates with the OpenAI Codex CLI /agent Plan-Apply mode export format — combined with the May 8 BNP Paribas Securities Services + Siemens Healthineers + Saudi Aramco Digital go-live cohort that lifted tenancy past 290, the Singapore IMDA / Japan AISI cyber-eval reciprocity perimeter now extended to South Korea PIPC + New Zealand GCSB inside the May 9 weekend extension, and the NHS England agentic-AI workflow-platform CVE blocklist naming LangGraph CVE-2026-44012 + LiteLLM CVE-2026-44188 + CrewAI CVE-2026-44352 + Haystack CVE-2026-44391 as disallowed pre-patch versions — force the next wave of EU central-government and allied-jurisdiction AI-orchestrator RFPs to name a Workflows-shaped sovereign-cloud tenancy clause (control-plane separation between tenant data and orchestrator runtime, sovereign-cloud execution-worker model with named-jurisdiction execution boundary, per-step token-budget bookkeeping interoperable with the OpenAI Codex CLI export format) as a baseline procurement-eligibility requirement rather than a discretionary scoring criterion. The forcing function is that once a flagship central-tax-administration estate cites the architecture by name as the decider against the two leading US alternatives, EU member-state procurement frameworks and Indo-Pacific reciprocity signatories have a defensible reference template they can require without authoring bespoke language. The most likely shape is a four-jurisdiction cohort (France DGFiP-equivalent + Germany BSI-equivalent + at least one Singapore/Japan signatory + at least one Five Eyes ally) treating sovereign-cloud control-plane separation plus execution-worker jurisdiction plus token-budget interop as the paired clauses; sovereign-cloud and FedRAMP-Moderate tenants adopt first because the AISI-administered cyber-eval reciprocity perimeter is already the operative threshold. Bear case is that AWS Bedrock Agent Registry's FedRAMP-Moderate inheritance plus the Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Governance Center reciprocity-attestation field add ships a hyperscaler-managed sovereign-cloud equivalent first; absent that, Q1 2027 lands the Workflows-shaped tenancy clause across the cohort.

reasoning.because: DGFiP picks Workflows citing control-plane separation + sovereign-cloud execution May 9.
reasoning.given: Indo-Pacific cyber-eval reciprocity perimeter + NHS England CVE blocklist set sovereign-cloud bar.
reasoning.so_that: Allied AI-orchestrator RFPs name a Workflows-shape sovereign-cloud tenancy clause as eligibility.
reasoning.landing: By Q1 2027; four jurisdictions (France + Germany + Indo-Pacific + Five Eyes).
reasoning.plain_language: France's tax agency picked Mistral over US tools, citing where the data lives; allied governments will copy that buying rule.

predictions.summary: Mistral Workflows lands DGFiP's central tax estate May 9 with sovereign-cloud control-plane separation cited as decider over US alternatives. By Q1 2027 EU + allied AI-orchestrator RFPs name the Workflows-shape sovereign-cloud tenancy clause as eligibility.
